III. Tests of Carbohydrate Absorption
Lactose Intolerance
Hydrogen 
Breath Test 
for Lactose 
(HBT-lactose)
Lactose loading (2 g/kg) in lactase 
deficiency allows bacterial me-
tabolism of lactose with produc-
tion of H2 gas. Breath analyzed 
for H2 by gas chromatography.
Breath H2 measured fasting and 0.5 
and 2 hours after dosing with lac-
tose; a significant increase is asso-
ciated with malabsorption.
Normal increase: 
,50 parts/million 
(i.e., ,50 ppm)
Lactose intolerance: 
50 ppm or greater
Bacterial overgrowth can cause 
false-positive results; consump-
tion of soluble fiber or legumes, 
and smoking are associated 
with H2 production; false-
negative results caused by  
antibiotics.
Lactose  
tolerance test
Lactose loading (50 g) followed by 
blood sampling at 5, 10, 30, 60, 
90, and 120 min after dose;  
glucose produced from lactose 
is assayed.
Lactase deficiency associated with 
,20 mg/dL increase in serum 
glucose.
